status: Introduced 2026-01-13, referred to Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee; no further action through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Establishes a surcharge on electric public utility service to certain data centers during certain periods and creates a "Grid Modernization Fund" within BPU; a direct ratepayer-cost-allocation measure. Reintroduction of 2024-2025 session's A6040, which did not advance.

status: Introduced 2026-01-13, referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee; no further action through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Prohibits agreements intended to conceal information concerning the development of data centers under the Municipal Land Use Law (MLUL); a local-zoning transparency measure. Reintroduction of 2024-2025 session's A6181.

status: Reported from Assembly Environment and Solid Waste Committee with amendments and referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee, 2026-03-16; no further action recorded through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Directs DEP to study short- and long-term effects of large-scale data center water use.

status: Introduced 2026-03-16, referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee; no further action recorded through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: "Clean Energy AI Incentivization Act"; directs BPU to create standards and incentives for AI data centers that bring self-sufficient clean energy.

sponsors: Asm. Gregory E. Myhre; Asm. Alex Sauickie; Asm. Paul Kanitra; Asw. Victoria A. Flynn; Asm. Gerry Scharfenberger
status: Introduced 2026-03-19, referred to Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee; no further action through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Requires certain State agencies to establish expedited approval and permitting procedures for artificial intelligence data centers powered by small modular nuclear reactors; a siting/permitting-track bill (companion S3639).

status: Introduced 2026-06-08, referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee; no further action through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Requires data center developers to disclose certain information to the public and elected officials before preliminary site plan consideration under the MLUL; a local-zoning transparency/notice measure.

sponsors: Asm. William F. Moen Jr. / (Senate companion S4402)
status: Introduced 2026-06-18, referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee
key_provisions: "Responsible Data Center Development and Resource Protection Act"; establishes a Statewide framework governing siting, land use approval, energy sourcing, water use, and environmental impacts of large-load data center development. This is the most comprehensive data-center siting/regulation bill of the 2026-2027 session and is directly on point for the moratorium/siting tracker.

status: Passed both houses 2026-01-12; pocket veto (bill not acted on by Governor before end of 221st Legislature) 2026-01-20
key_provisions: Would have required large-load data center tariff protections for customers above 100 MW monthly demand.
Requires BPU study and report on data center electricity cost impacts.

sponsors: Asm. David Bailey Jr.; Asm. Joe Danielsen; Asm. Clinton Calabrese; Asw. Eliana Pintor Marin / Sen. John J. Burzichelli; Sen. John F. McKeon
status: A796 passed the Assembly 2026-03-23, substituted for S731 and passed both houses 2026-06-30, and was enacted as P.L.2026, c.32 on 2026-07-07
key_provisions: Requires electric public utilities to file tariffs for large load data centers at or above 100 MW peak load; assigns attributable costs to data centers and requires financial guarantees to protect other ratepayers.

sponsors: Sen. M. Teresa Ruiz; Sen. Raj Mukherji / Asm. Michael Venezia / Asw. Eliana Pintor Marin
status: S3379 amended and passed the Senate, then amended in Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities, substituted for A4096, and passed both houses 2026-06-30; awaiting gubernatorial action as of 2026-07-31. Companion A4696 (identical to separate bill S2274, not part of the S3379/A4096 pairing) remains in Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee since introduction 2026-03-16
key_provisions: Requires semi-annual data center water and energy usage reports to BPU for three years, with performance metrics for data centers receiving state incentives.

status: Introduced 2026-02-19, referred to Senate Community and Urban Affairs Committee; no further action recorded through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Amends the MLUL to require planning boards to submit certain data center applications to the State Planning Commission and BPU; requires State Planning Commission approval; excludes data centers from economic development subsidies.

status: Passed both houses 2025-06-30; conditionally vetoed 2025-10-20; the 221st Legislature adjourned in January 2026 without the Legislature ever concurring in the Governor's recommendations or overriding the veto, so the bill died with the conditional veto unresolved
key_provisions: Would require data center owners and operators to report water and energy usage to BPU.
Applies prevailing wage requirements to certain data center construction activity.

sponsors: Sen. Bob Smith; Sen. John F. McKeon / Asm. Joe Danielsen
status: S680 reported from Senate Environment and Energy Committee and referred to Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee 2026-03-16; companion A1170 has only its 2026-01-13 introduction and Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee referral recorded; no further action on either through 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Requires BPU approval of energy usage plans for proposed AI data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities; requires electricity from new clean energy sources after a PJM-region trigger is met.

sponsors: Sen. Bob Smith; Sen. Linda Greenstein
status: Reported from Senate Environment and Energy Committee 2026-03-16; resolution passed by the full Senate 2026-03-23 (22-15) and filed with the Secretary of State 2026-03-23
key_provisions: Urges PJM-region states and the District of Columbia to adopt policies requiring data centers to obtain electricity from new zero- or low-emission sources.
